chapter_name: The Origin and Evolution of the Earth
learning_objective: 🎯 Travel back in time 13.7 billion years! Discover how a massive explosion created the universe, and how stardust eventually formed our beautiful blue planet.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This is the most accepted theory for the origin of the universe. About 13.7 billion years ago, all matter was in one tiny, infinitely hot point. It exploded with a 'Big Bang', expanding rapidly to create the universe.
A nebula is a giant cloud of gas (mostly hydrogen) and dust in space. Gravity causes this cloud to collapse and spin, generating intense heat and eventually forming luminous stars.
Around a star, gas and dust form a spinning disc. Matter clumps together into small bodies called 'planetesimals'. These planetesimals collide and join together due to gravity to form planets.

Earth started as a barren, rocky, hot ball. Through 'differentiation', heavy metals sank to the core and lighter materials formed the crust. 'Degassing' from volcanoes released water vapour and gases, forming the atmosphere and oceans.

fun_activity.title: 🎈 The Expanding Universe Balloon
fun_activity.instructions: Take a deflated balloon and draw some dots on it with a marker (these are galaxies). Now, blow up the balloon. Notice how the dots move away from EACH OTHER as the balloon expands. This is exactly how the universe is expanding right now!

exam_tips: 📌 Terrestrial Planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are rocky and small. Jovian Planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) are gaseous and huge. Know the difference!
📌 The 'Nebular Hypothesis' was proposed by Immanuel Kant and revised by Laplace.
📌 'Degassing' is a crucial term. It explains how the early Earth's atmosphere was formed through the release of gases from the Earth's interior.
quick_recap: ⭐ The universe began with the Big Bang around 13.7 billion years ago and is still expanding.
⭐ Earth's layered structure (core, mantle, crust) formed through a process called differentiation.
⭐ Our oceans formed when early Earth cooled, causing water vapour to condense and rain for thousands of years.
